name: Perfect Citizen: A Novel of the Meridian
creator: Stellan Adeyemi-Cruz
description: A slick, propulsive thriller published by Helix Consolidated's literary imprint, following a Tier 3 compliance officer who uncovers what appears to be a terrorist cell operating through pirated neural feed channels — only to discover, in a twist the corporate publisher apparently did not fully anticipate, that the 'terrorists' are a family trying to free a member from an illegal debt-indenture augmentation contract. The novel's ending was modified between the first and second print runs, softening the protagonist's final moral choice.
medium: licensed neural feed (primary) and physical book (mass market)
cultural_impact: The existence of two distinct endings became a cultural scandal that drew more attention to debt-indenture augmentation than any advocacy campaign had managed; readers began trading first-edition physical copies specifically for the original ending.
controversy: Author Adeyemi-Cruz has never publicly confirmed or denied that the ending was changed under publisher pressure; the first-run physical copies are now actively collected, and Helix Consolidated has declined to reprint them.
story_hooks: A first-run copy has surfaced with a third manuscript page tucked inside, handwritten, that appears to be the author's original intended final scene — and it implicates a real corponation, not a fictional one.
Adeyemi-Cruz has been contracted for a sequel, but sources suggest they are writing two versions simultaneously with the intention of leaking the uncensored one.
A film adaptation is in production, and the director has publicly committed to using the original ending — leading to what may be a very public legal confrontation with Helix Consolidated.
